hub.title: Slang Dictionary: Chinese and English Internet Slang Meanings
hub.description: What does yyds, neijuan, emo, PUA, rizz or 6 7 mean? A slang dictionary of {n} Chinese and English internet words, each with its meaning, origin, real examples and similar words.
hub.lede: Short, sourced answers to "what does it mean?" for the Chinese and English internet words people search most: number codes, pinyin abbreviations, work and life buzzwords, moods, dating talk and English slang.
about: Every entry answers the question first, then explains where the word came from, shows how people use it in chats and comments, and compares it with words that mean something close.

Words were picked from what people actually search for, and origins are checked against dictionaries, official word-of-the-year lists and other public sources. Slang moves fast, so each page shows when it was last updated.

faq.a: Words, abbreviations, numbers and memes that spread through chats, comments and short videos, such as yyds in Chinese or rizz in English. Many fade within a year; some, like 内卷 (neijuan), reach newspapers and dictionaries.

faq.q: Why do Chinese netizens use numbers and letters?
faq.a: Numbers sound like words (520 sounds like "I love you" in Mandarin) and pinyin initials are fast to type (yyds is yong yuan de shen). They are quicker to write and feel like an in-group joke.

faq.q: Is it OK to use these words at work?
faq.a: Most are casual. Playful ones like 666 or yyds are fine with friends, while words that judge people, such as 渣男 or simp, can offend. Each entry has a note on tone.
